approach: Make the learner write first on every case. Fields that ask for judgment (reader, voice patterns, edit) start empty, with short placeholder hints. The prepared answer, the three reasons, and the prepared voice patterns stay in collapsed details labeled as prepared by the coach. Opening them is always allowed. Once opened, they sit beside the learner's attempt so the comparison is direct. Fictional facts and fictional voice samples stay prefilled because they are source material, not answers. The builder then turns the learner's own choices into reusable instructions, which they test on a second brief. Two things are being practiced and they are named separately: the instructions (a reusable skill file) and the judgment behind them (noticing what a reader needs and what the facts support).
heading: Practice: write for one reader, then write instructions you can reuse
intro: This is a practice room with fictional organizations, facts, and drafts. Nothing you type is sent anywhere, graded, or checked by a tool. You do the attempt first. Prepared examples are here if you want them, and every one is marked as prepared.

exerciseSteps.title: 1. Pick the reader
exerciseSteps.instruction: Read the brief and the source facts. In one or two sentences, say who will read this and what they need to decide or do after reading.

exerciseSteps.title: 2. Find the voice in the samples
exerciseSteps.instruction: Read the three fictional voice samples. Write three to five patterns you notice, such as sentence length, how numbers are stated, how students are described, and what the writer avoids.

exerciseSteps.title: 3. Check and edit the flawed draft
exerciseSteps.instruction: Compare each claim in the draft against the source facts. Mark anything the facts do not support, then rewrite the passage in your own words.

exerciseSteps.title: 4. Test your instructions on a new brief
exerciseSteps.instruction: Copy the instructions the builder assembles from your answers. Use them on the second brief and note which lines helped and which were missing or too vague.

attemptHint: Start with the claims. Does each number match the source facts? Is anything stated as known that the facts leave open?
comparePrompt: Put your edit next to the prepared version. Where did you catch the same problem? Where did you choose differently, and can you point to a source fact that supports your choice?
voicePrompt: What patterns do you see across these samples?
voiceHint: Write each pattern as something a writer could follow. For example: "States amounts as exact figures, never rounded up." Avoid broad labels like "warm" unless you say what makes it warm.
preparedVoiceLabel: Prepared voice patterns (written by the coach, open to compare)
builderIntro: This section collects what you wrote above into one set of instructions. Edit anything. These instructions are your reusable skill. The judgment you used to write them is the other half, and you bring that with you to each new piece.
coachNote: Let the learner keep the keyboard. If they are stuck for more than a minute or two, point them to the prepared starting guide rather than typing for them. Ask what they noticed in the facts before they open a prepared answer. Do not ask for real organization samples. The fictional ones are enough to practice the method, and the learner can apply the same steps to their own material later.
homeIntro: Practice turning grant and donor writing into a method you can repeat. You will choose a reader, pull voice patterns from samples, check a draft against facts, and test your own instructions on a second brief. All cases are fictional.
implementationNotes: Default field states: reader, voice patterns, avoid list, and the draft edit start empty with placeholders. Org name, source facts, fictional voice samples, audience, and format stay prefilled as source material.
Prepared answer, three reasons, and prepared voice patterns go in collapsed <details> with a 'Prepared by the coach' label. Nothing is locked. Opening them is not tracked.
Optional 'Prepared starting guide' button fills only blank fields, and each filled field gets a visible 'from guide' tag until the learner edits it.
Reset: clears learner-entered text for the current case only and restores prefilled source fields. It asks for confirmation if any learner text exists.
Case switching: keep each tab's drafts separately in memory (sessionStorage only). Switching does not clear drafts, and a small 'your draft saved' note appears on return.
Preserve corrections: the facts state no eligible-applicant count, the draft must not infer the fund is exhausted, and the essay topic is shown as 'Unknown, confirm with funder'.
Markdown preview, copy, and download use the learner's text. Empty sections render as '[not written yet]' and are not filled from prepared examples.
Add offline checks so that fields start empty, details start collapsed, reset only affects the current case, drafts survive tab switches, nothing is sent over the network, and no score is displayed.
